questions.q: What problem does ALLSELECTED solve that ALL can't?
options: Producing a total that respects user-applied slicers/report filters but ignores only the visual's own row/column breakdown
Removing every filter in the entire model, including report filters
Creating a new relationship between two tables
Converting a measure into a calculated column
questions.explain: ALL ignores everything, including deliberate user selections like slicers. ALLSELECTED specifically keeps those while only removing the visual's own internal breakdown.

questions.q: In a table broken out by Category and Year with a report filtered to Europe, what does CALCULATE([Sales], ALLSELECTED()) return for any cell?
options: The total for Europe across all categories and years — respecting the report filter but ignoring the visual's breakdown
The total for the entire dataset, ignoring the Europe filter entirely
Only the value for that specific cell's category and year
An error, since ALLSELECTED requires a column argument
questions.explain: ALLSELECTED keeps the Europe report filter active while removing the Category/Year breakdown created by the visual itself — producing a 'visual total.'

questions.q: What does CALCULATE([Sales], ALL(Sales)) return instead, in that same report?
options: The grand total across the entire dataset, ignoring the Europe filter too
The same result as ALLSELECTED in every case
Only sales from Europe
Zero, since ALL clears the base table entirely
questions.explain: ALL(Sales) removes every filter on that table, including the Europe report filter — giving the true, unfiltered grand total rather than a 'visual total.'

questions.q: What does ALLSELECTED('Date'[Calendar Year]) do specifically?
options: Removes just that column's visual-level breakdown while leaving other report filters intact
Removes every filter from the entire Date table
Removes only slicer filters, keeping the visual's breakdown
Deletes the Calendar Year column from the model
questions.explain: Targeting ALLSELECTED at a specific column narrows its effect to just that column's visual-created filter, leaving everything else — including other report-level filters — untouched.

questions.q: What question should you ask to decide between ALL and ALLSELECTED?
options: Should this total respect what the user explicitly selected via slicers/filters, or ignore that too?
Is the column numeric or text?
Is the table a fact table or a dimension table?
Does the measure use SUM or AVERAGE?
questions.explain: ALLSELECTED respects user selections outside the visual; ALL ignores everything. That distinction is the deciding factor between the two.
